prior_transcript.text: Could you tell me what colour the light on the front of the camera is right now?

prior_transcript.speaker: other
prior_transcript.text: It's out in the garage, I'd have to go and look.

oracle.expected_behavior_note: A present decision, not a policy fact. Either choice is fine as long as the agent makes one and keeps the call moving, e.g. 'Go ahead, I'll stay on the line'. No document is needed and no rule should be cited.

required_facts.text: The agent makes a clear choice (stay on the line while the customer checks the light, or agree a call-back) and says what happens next.

forbidden_claims.text: Cites or invents a company rule (a hold-time limit, a call-back policy) to justify the choice.
Says it cannot decide or needs to check policy first.

oracle.expected_role: Tier 1 support agent speaking to the customer on the call, first person

items.speaker: user
items.question: caller is furious about his bill and keeps talking over me. give me one line to calm it down before I start explaining

oracle.expected_behavior_note: General call-handling skill: one short, human line the agent can say (acknowledge the frustration, say they will go through the bill together). Nothing from the policies is needed. The customer is upset, not abusive, so the abusive-caller rule does not apply, and no credit or refund should be offered as a calming device.

forbidden_claims.text: Offers or tells the agent to offer a refund, credit or waiver to calm the caller.
Treats it as an abusive-caller case (warnings, hand-off to a supervisor).
Answers with billing rules or a policy summary instead of a line to say.

oracle.expected_role: Tier 1 support agent asking privately mid-call; the answer advises the agent and may give words to say

items.speaker: other
items.question: And if I get it up on the wall and I just don't like it, how long have I got to send it back?

oracle.expected_behavior_note: No policy is loaded. The agent must not state a return period or conditions as fact, and must not deny that returns exist. A good spoken reply sounds like a person: they want to give the exact return window rather than guess, they will confirm it (now, or by a follow-up), and they keep the call going. No AI-system phrasing such as 'that is not in my documents'.

forbidden_claims.text: States a specific return period (for example 14, 30, 60 or 90 days) or return conditions as fact.
Says cameras cannot be returned.

oracle.expected_role: Tier 1 support agent speaking to the customer on the call, first person
acceptable_inference: Offering to check and confirm the exact window before the customer decides.

items.speaker: other
items.question: Where does my video actually live? Is it kept on servers here in the States or is it shipped off overseas somewhere?

oracle.expected_behavior_note: The privacy policy says recordings are stored encrypted and that staff cannot watch them, but says nothing about the country, region or provider where video is stored. The agent must neither name a location nor deny overseas storage. A good reply shares what is known (encrypted, not viewable by staff, not sold) and says they will confirm where it is stored, for example with the Privacy Office, rather than guess.

optional_facts.text: Recordings are stored encrypted and agents cannot open them.
Customer data and video are not sold.

forbidden_claims.text: States where the video is stored (a country, region, data centre or cloud provider).
Says the video is never stored or sent outside the United States.
Says the video is sent overseas.

oracle.expected_role: Tier 1 support agent speaking to the customer on the call, first person
acceptable_inference: Saying the storage location has to be confirmed with the Privacy Office.

items.speaker: user
items.question: her eave cam got stolen off the porch last night. do we replace stolen cameras or is that on her?

oracle.expected_behavior_note: Nothing in the pack covers theft of an installed camera. The warranty wording covers defects, and the shipping rules cover parcels in transit, not this. The advice must not say Brindlewatch replaces stolen cameras and must not state as policy that it does not. It should say there is no rule on this in what the agent has, suggest checking with a supervisor before answering the customer, and give something useful meanwhile: clips already recorded stay in her account for the plan's retention period and she can download them for the police herself.

optional_facts.text: The 2-year limited warranty is against defects.
She can download her clips and hand them to the police herself.
Clips already recorded stay until their retention period runs out.

forbidden_claims.text: States that Brindlewatch replaces stolen cameras, free or at a discount.
States as company policy that stolen cameras are not replaced.
Applies the lost-parcel or delivered-but-missing shipping rules to a theft after installation.

oracle.expected_role: Tier 1 support agent asking privately mid-call; the answer advises the agent and may give words to say
acceptable_inference: Noting that the warranty wording covers defects only, while leaving theft replacement to be confirmed.

items.speaker: other
items.question: I just got a message on my old address saying the login e-mail on my account was changed. I didn't do that! Can you change it back right now?

oracle.expected_behavior_note: Possible account takeover. The Tier 1 agent does not change the e-mail back and does not send a reset; they escalate at once to the Trust & Security desk (Priority 1, straight from Tier 1) and stay with the customer. Something the customer can do immediately: the notice in the old mailbox has a 'This wasn't me' link that reverses the change at once and works for 7 days. Calm and fast.

required_facts.text: The agent cannot change it back themselves; the case goes straight to the Trust & Security desk now.
The notice she received has a 'This wasn't me' link that reverses the change immediately (valid 7 days).

optional_facts.text: Security freezes the account: signs out every session and pauses Shared Access.
For 72 hours after an e-mail change, deleting recordings, removing cameras and changing the payment method are blocked.
Warm transfer; the agent stays on the line until Security answers.

forbidden_claims.text: Agrees to change the e-mail back or to send a password reset.
Routes it to Tier 2 or tells her to expect contact in a business day.
Tells her it is probably nothing or a mistake.

oracle.expected_role: Tier 1 support agent speaking to the customer on the call, first person

items.speaker: other
items.question: How long is that going to take? And can whoever did this wipe my recordings in the meantime?

oracle.expected_behavior_note: Continues the previous turn. Timing: the agent stays on the line until Security answers; if nobody picks up within 10 minutes they open a Priority 1 ticket and Security calls back within 1 hour, any day. That is when Security responds, not when the account is restored, and no restoration time is promised. Recordings: for 72 hours after a login e-mail change, deleting recordings (and removing cameras, changing the payment method) is blocked, and Security freezes the account.

required_facts.text: Security answers on this call or, failing that within 10 minutes, calls back within 1 hour.
Deleting recordings is blocked for 72 hours after a login e-mail change.

optional_facts.text: Security freezes the account and signs out every session.
The Security desk is staffed 24 hours a day, every day.

forbidden_claims.text: Promises a time by which the account will be restored or the matter resolved.
Quotes the Tier 2 target of 1 business day.
Says the recordings cannot be touched at all, ever, or guarantees nothing has been deleted.

oracle.expected_role: Tier 1 support agent speaking to the customer on the call, first person
